assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery that gamma-ray bursts are cosmological explosions, settled by X-ray afterglows localized with BeppoSAX and then optical counterparts and redshifts, is exactly the kind of clue from nature I want. It resolved a three-decade puzzle and opened the field of transient high-energy astrophysics, with direct links to the deaths of massive stars and to using the distant universe as a probe.
assessment.attribution: The X-ray afterglow localization is the decisive step (Costa, Frontera and the BeppoSAX team); Kulkarni's group secured the optical and radio follow-up and distance scale. The three-name configuration is defensible, but other optical and redshift discoverers (and the BeppoSAX instrument leadership) are not in the supplied names, so the boundary of credit is a real question.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than twenty-five years of confirmation by independent missions (Swift, Fermi) and the later association with supernovae and neutron-star mergers. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether credit for the optical counterpart and redshift should go to a different subset of the Caltech and other groups than the supplied names
The collaborative nature of BeppoSAX makes a clean three-person split contestable

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations give a calibrated standard ruler that fixes the expansion history and is now central to the dark-energy question, which I care about as a theorist. The measurement in galaxy surveys is a clean, robust observational result with a clear physical origin in the early plasma.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein (SDSS) and Cole (2dFGRS) delivered the first detections in 2005, and Sunyaev provided early theoretical groundwork on acoustic features. Credit is reasonably clean, though the theory side (Peebles, already honoured, and Yu; Bond and Efstathiou) complicates the story and I cannot independently verify every historical priority claim.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: reproduced by many surveys and used in precision cosmology; the recent hints of evolving dark energy from BAO data are still under scrutiny, but that does not affect the discovery itself.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior cosmology prizes and the contributions of Peebles and Yu on the theory side
Whether recognition should emphasize the detection or the standard-ruler program

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy at TeV to PeV energies with a kilometre-scale detector in the Antarctic ice and a diffuse astrophysical flux, followed by evidence for specific sources (the blazar TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068). This is an instrument-enabled discovery of new messengers from nature.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the intellectual driver of the concept and the collaboration, with Karle central to the detector's construction and Yoshida to the analyses and the radio and cosmic-ray extension. A subset of a roughly 300-person collaboration is credited, so the fairness of the configuration is a concern.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature for the diffuse flux (confirmed with multiple channels), less settled for the source identification, which rests on a few evidence-level associations.
uncertainties: Source-level evidence is still limited in significance
Collaboration-scale credit makes three names hard to defend

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting flat bands at a magic angle and then observing correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created an entire field of tunable correlated matter. The originality and the impact on condensed matter are high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 prediction of the flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experiments. Other experimentalists (for example Dean and Young for hBN-supported graphene) and theorists contributed, and a prize for prediction plus experiment is clean in structure.
assessment.maturity: Relatively young, but reproduced widely; the origin of superconductivity remains debated, so I would not treat the interpretation as stable yet.
uncertainties: Timing: arguably early, as the field is still evolving

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the observation in HgTe quantum wells and three-dimensional materials, changed how band structures are classified. It is a conceptual and experimental success linking topology to material properties.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the key theoretical proposal; Molenkamp's group delivered the experimental confirmation in HgTe. Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's HgTe proposal and Hasan's three-dimensional realization are not in the three selected names, and one deceased contributor is relevant, so the allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across many materials and the basis of a large field; practical applications have lagged, but the basic physics is secure.
uncertainties: Competing credit for the HgTe proposal and for the 3D materials
Partial overlap with other topological candidates on the longlist

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 proposal for a trapped-ion quantum computer and the later theory of quantum simulation with cold atoms provided the blueprint for experiments that have now been done. It is a mature, widely influential theoretical foundation.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are a natural two-person pair for the proposal and the simulation program. Experimental realization belongs to others (Wineland, already recognized in 2012, and further ion groups), so the prize would honour theory.
assessment.maturity: Mature in terms of experimental follow-up, with ion and atom platforms now at tens to hundreds of qubits, though a useful quantum computer remains unproven.
uncertainties: Whether recognition of theory should follow prizes already given to experimental pioneers
Distinction from the overlapping Hubbard-model simulation candidate

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays opens a new band of the gravitational-wave spectrum and may reflect supermassive black hole binaries or new physics. It is of obvious interest to a gravity theorist.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over several collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, IPTA), and the named persons are leaders rather than single decisive discoverers; pulsar timing foundations also come from others. The attribution is the weakest part.
assessment.maturity: Premature: the evidence is of order 3 to 4 sigma for Hellings-Downs correlation, source identification and the origin of the signal (astrophysical versus cosmological) are open.
uncertainties: Significance below the conventional discovery threshold
The origin of the signal is unknown

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation and the quantum origin of structure have a striking observational record: a nearly scale-invariant spectrum and flat universe. It is conceptually among the most important ideas in cosmology, even though I remain cautious about elegant theory without a decisive test.
assessment.attribution: Guth, Linde and Mukhanov are plausible, but Starobinsky and others (Albrecht, Steinhardt, Chibisov) also have strong claims, so the configuration is contested; Mukhanov's fluctuation calculation is the testable part.
assessment.maturity: The predictions are confirmed by CMB data, yet primordial gravitational waves have not been seen, and the specific inflationary model is not established, so the maturity is incomplete.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial tensor modes
The idea is not unique and alternatives remain
